_source: kotilabs/aagman-content-layer2 — voice/ overlays, prompts/, README content rules, and approved final/ output. Lengths are the repo's stated targets; where the repo gives a range it is preserved.

substack_blog.length: long-form; opening analogy fixed at 100-150 words; no hard word cap (quality/signal-driven, not quota)
structure: implications for decision-makers (incl. 'what this does NOT affect')
substack_blog.sourcing: full source table with # / source / title / date / URL; read full source before citing; charts label source, timeframe, units, nominal-vs-real
substack_blog.disclosure: structural: no price targets, no buy/sell, explicit 'does not tell anyone what to buy or sell', open-question ending. Harness adds: explicit educational/not-advice line (see sebi_extras.md)
substack_blog.seo_aeo: blog-only audit. Title/H1 honest no clickbait; meta description 150-160 chars stating tension/question, no false urgency; H2s phrased as reader/AI questions; direct answer in first 100 words; quotable 40-60 word paragraphs
substack_blog.ending: open question / tension worth watching — never CTA or conclusion

x_thread.length: 8-15 posts; each post under ~250 characters where possible
structure: Post 1 hook: name the shift not the topic, one sharp sentence
body posts: one idea per post, one beat each
mid-thread pivot: name thesis ('This isn't X. It's Y.')
final post: open cognitive tension, no CTA
x_thread.links: no link in the first post
x_thread.sourcing: numbers specific and sourced inline; each post standalone-quotable (screenshot test)
x_thread.disclosure: structural (no tips/targets/promises); harness adds not-advice line on the thread's profile/pinned or final post per channel policy
x_thread.ending: unresolved tension — no 'follow for more', no CTA

linkedin_carousel.register: slightly more formal than Instagram; headlines can be longer; named institutions and data callouts land well
per_slide: hero stat or quote with source
speaker note (what the slide does in the argument)
linkedin_carousel.structure: lead concrete then abstract; exactly one explicit pivot slide mid-deck ('This isn't X, it's Y'); vary slide weight (dense evidence slide earns a sparse one-liner)
linkedin_carousel.hashtags: none (repo carries no hashtags on carousels)
linkedin_carousel.last_slide: promo → link to Substack with one sentence on the open question; standalone → the open question, NO external link
linkedin_carousel.sourcing: numbers sourced inline on the hero-stat line
linkedin_carousel.disclosure: structural + harness not-advice line on the deck (e.g. final/back slide)
linkedin_carousel.italics: sparingly — max one conceptual word per slide; em dashes for pivots

instagram_carousel.register: more visual rhythm; SHORTER headlines than LinkedIn; design notes matter more (image content, colour contrast, minimal text per slide)
instagram_carousel.structure: same argument arc as LinkedIn; even more concise
instagram_carousel.last_slide: same as LinkedIn but even more concise; standalone → no link
instagram_carousel.forbidden: rhetorical questions mid-deck, 'Imagine if…', 'The future of X', exclamation marks, emoji, hype openers, engagement bait

infographic_concepts.length: surface the most interesting verified numbers + 3-5 specific concepts
mandatory_sections: 'Verified interesting data' table with per-datapoint verdict
source-definition line where estimates differ by segment/date
infographic_concepts.disclosure: visual ideas must rest on verified numbers; caveat lines and 'used for perspective, not prediction' captions required; no fabricated data
